question: A 48-year-old woman with alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency undergoes a lung transplant. She tolerates the surgery well, but 3 years later develops inflammation and fibrosis in her terminal bronchioles. Which of the following best describes the pathophysiology of this patient's deterioration?

options.opb: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes reacting against foreign MHCs
options.opc: Lymphocytic inflammation of the bronchiolar wall
options.ope: Proliferation of grafted immunocompetent T cells

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency -> Lung transplant -> Chronic rejection -> Inflammation and fibrosis in terminal bronchioles -> Lymphocytic inflammation of the bronchiolar wall -> 80% CHAIN: Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency -> Lung transplant -> Immunosuppressive therapy -> Immune system imbalance -> Proliferation of grafted immunocompetent T cells -> 80%
analysis: The patient's deterioration is most likely due to chronic rejection, which is characterized by lymphocytic inflammation of the bronchiolar wall leading to fibrosis. This is a common complication following lung transplantation.
